sentences: A doubling metric has uniformly limited local branching: each ball can be covered by a bounded number of smaller balls.
The Lang–Plaut problem considers such a metric when it already sits inside a Hilbert space.
It asks whether the points can be represented in some finite-dimensional Euclidean space while changing all distances by only a bounded factor.
Both dimension and distortion should depend only on the doubling constant.
The issue is whether intrinsic metric simplicity suffices to eliminate an infinite-dimensional ambient representation.
